unreadable: OpenSSL cannot read this certificate, so no handshake uses it.
sourceFileTip: Loaded from tls.trustAnchorsFile at startup. Removing it here lasts until the next start, when the file is read again.
sourceRuntimeStoredTip: Added at runtime and written to ou=trustAnchors, so it survives a restart wherever the directory is persisted.
sourceRuntimeUnstoredTip: Added at runtime and NOT written down — the directory was full or no store is installed — so it is gone at the next start.
removeFileTip: Stops client certificates chaining only to this anchor from verifying, until the next start re-reads tls.trustAnchorsFile.
removeRuntimeTip: Stops client certificates chaining only to this anchor from verifying. Nothing brings it back.
empty: Empty. No client certificate verifies on any listener, so every one presented arrives UNVERIFIED and everything that reads one refuses it.
intro: Every anchor LDAPS 636 and the main port verify a client certificate against. A certificate that chains to one of these is VERIFIED — and since 2026-09-06 a verified certificate is an identity here: it starts a sign-on session, and it is what admits a remote XACML PEP to /xacml/pep/*. So this list decides whose certificates this service believes.
fileSet: tls.trustAnchorsFile is {file}, and {n} anchor(s) were loaded from it at startup.
fileUnset: tls.trustAnchorsFile is not set, so every anchor here was added while this process was running.
controlsOpen: answer anybody in this development-mode process.
controlsRefused: are refused in product mode; this page and /admin-api/tls/trust are the runtime doors.
addNote: One or more -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- blocks — the root, or the whole chain above the leaf. Every block must be one OpenSSL can read, or NONE is added: a block the listener cannot parse makes the next truststore change throw on every listener. A certificate already held is counted and not added twice.
noButton: What there is deliberately no button for
noClear: Emptying the truststore. A bulk clear on this door would be the one control whose reach is every client certificate every other caller relies on — a remote PEP authenticating as nobody for the rest of a run is what one unguarded clear has already cost. Remove the rows you mean, one at a time; the ones you did not put there are the ones you have to name. Removing a file anchor is allowed and lasts until the next start.
linkApi: the same over the management API
